rules.statement: A code comment that cites a decision record (for example "See ADR-NNNN") must point to a record that exists in the repository or is added in the same change; otherwise drop the reference and put the reasoning in the comment.
rules.why: A reader who follows a dangling reference finds nothing, and the reasoning behind the code is recorded nowhere.
rules.check: For each new or changed comment citing an ADR number, confirm a matching docs/decisions file exists or is added by the diff and that the cited number is the right record.

rules.statement: In a test project, a helper that keeps advancing a fake clock or polling until a task completes must stop at a wall-clock deadline (for example measured with Stopwatch.GetTimestamp/GetElapsedTime) and fail the test with the task's state, rather than loop without a limit or stop after a fixed number of steps.
rules.why: An unbounded loop makes CI hang until the job times out instead of failing a named test, and a fixed step count can run out before a passing continuation on the thread pool completes, which makes the test flaky.
rules.check: Look for `while (!task.IsCompleted)` style loops in test helpers that advance time or yield; verify they have a wall-clock deadline and call Assert.Fail or throw when it passes, and that the bound isn't a fixed iteration count.

rules.statement: In production code, a service shouldn't create its own private instance of a type that is registered as a shared singleton (such as a lock table) with `new()`; inject the shared instance through the constructor and keep separate uses apart with a key that includes their purpose.
rules.why: Private instances can't be substituted in tests, their separation is enforced only by convention, and injecting the shared one later would silently merge their key spaces.
rules.check: Look for fields initialised with `new()` for types that are also registered in DI as singletons; check whether the instance is injected and whether keys from different users are separated by a purpose component.

rules.statement: Don't report a per-replica cache in a singleton as unbounded or as a violation of the stateless-singleton rule when its keys come only from configuration (never from request data), correctness doesn't depend on it, and an ADR records it as an accepted exception.
rules.why: Such a cache holds at most one entry per configured key, and a replica that misses or restarts just recomputes the value, so it neither grows without bound nor needs shared state.
rules.check: Before reporting, trace where the cache keys come from (configuration vs request values), check whether a miss only causes a recomputation, and look for an ADR recording the exception.
